confirmed_facts.claim: Circle's Q2 2026 SEC filing defines 'USDC on platform' as Circle's own Circle Mint accounts, corporate-held USDC and non-custodial wallets offered through Circle. The 19.5% daily weighted-average share is Circle's platform share, not Coinbase's.

Circle Mint customer initiated fiat conversions in Q2 2026 were USD83.004B minted and USD86.784B redeemed, net -USD3.780B. H1 2026 was USD156.543B minted and USD158.540B redeemed, net -USD1.997B. These are Circle Mint customer flows, not total USDC secondary-market activity.

Circle incurred USD324.6M Q2 and USD655.3M H1 2026 distribution costs in connection with Coinbase agreements. The agreement's allocation mechanics reference USDC held on Coinbase's platform after issuer retention and a share of remaining ecosystem growth after approved third-party participant payments.

Coinbase's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q says it renewed its arrangement with Circle Internet Financial, LLC on the same terms. Coinbase reported Q3 stablecoin revenue of USD306.905M versus USD324.534M in Q3 2025, a 5% decline. Corporate payment-stablecoin balance interest was reclassified to Other revenue beginning Q1 2026, so the stablecoin-revenue line must be interpreted with the filing's presentation note.

Coinbase's Q3 2026 recognized lending collateral was USD1.009297B, comprising USD997.557M crypto and USD11.740M fiat/payment stablecoins. The crypto table names BTC USD920.649M and ETH USD67.005M, with USD9.903M in aggregate 'other crypto assets'. Recognized derivatives collateral was USD301.943M, consisting of BTC USD298.212M and ETH USD3.731M; collateral requirements were at least 100% of derivative notional.

Coinbase separately disclosed USD3.284562B customer collateral not recognized as an asset or obligation to return, including USD2.804112B crypto and USD480.450M fiat/payment stablecoins, without a token-level breakdown. Company assets pledged against short-term borrowings were USD434.163M and are a separate encumbrance view, not an additional independent collateral pool.

The Coinbase Q3 2026 10-Q contains no XRP-specific collateral amount and its recognized derivatives-collateral table names BTC and ETH only. The filing does not establish zero XRP exposure across all customer collateral or custody; the USD9.903M 'other crypto' lending category and USD2.804112B unrecognized customer crypto collateral are not token-itemized.

inferences: Coinbase-Circle distribution economics are materially linked to Coinbase-platform USDC balances and broader ecosystem growth; Coinbase's Q3 filing confirms the arrangement was renewed on the same terms.
Circle's 19.5% on-platform metric cannot be used as Coinbase's share. Coinbase's platform balance share must be measured separately from Circle's own platform metric.

The Q3 recognized derivatives-collateral disclosure does not evidence XRP collateral at Coinbase. A material XRP amount in recognized lending collateral is also not evidenced by the filing, but the aggregate 'other crypto' category prevents an absolute zero-exposure conclusion.
The unrecognized USD2.804112B customer crypto collateral pool is not token-itemized and cannot be assigned to XRP or any other asset from this filing.

Circle Mint net redemptions in Q2 do not by themselves establish contraction in total USDC supply or predict XRP demand; the measure covers Circle Mint customer conversions and excludes a complete view of secondary-market and other distributor activity.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase remains a strategically important USDC distributor whose economics are linked to Coinbase-held USDC and broader ecosystem growth.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The precise Coinbase platform-share percentage and Q3 settlement amounts under the agreement are not disclosed in these captured materials. Circle's 19.5% metric is Circle's own platform share, not Coinbase's.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase has material XRP collateral exposure in its Q3 2026 recognized institutional lending or derivatives book.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The recognized derivatives table names BTC and ETH only. Recognized lending 'other crypto assets' totals USD9.903M without asset breakdown; the unrecognized USD2.804112B customer crypto collateral is not token-itemized. No XRP-specific amount is disclosed.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle Mint net issuance/redemption flows can serve as a leading indicator of XRP demand through stablecoin settlement or bridge activity.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: The metric is Circle Mint customer fiat conversion activity, not all USDC supply/secondary-market activity. No XRPL route-level USDC/RLUSD-to-XRP conversion or XRP bridge flow is measured. Circle Arc and other rails can settle stablecoins without native XRP.
